prose: A case study in agent-assisted performance engineering: for Kimi K3, the team used coding agents to write complex GPU kernels, cross-operator fusions and computation-communication overlap, building a unified CuTe DSL decode path on the NVIDIA GB300 covering attention, MoE and communication across 8 or 16 GPUs. Results: over 840 tokens/s at batch 1 on 16 GB300s with DSpark, 1.5-2x higher decode throughput in several configurations, and up to 1.8x higher P90 interactivity on the AgentX workload.

The honest second half: agent-optimized inference code is outpacing the review and maintenance workflow. Manually understanding every kernel line and testing every configuration doesn't scale, but skipping it risks shipping production bugs - so the team argues performance work itself must be reorganized around automatic verification of reliability alongside agentic optimization.
highlights: Agent-written GPU kernels for Kimi K3 in vLLM on NVIDIA GB300
840+ tokens/s at batch 1 on 16 GPUs with DSpark
1.5-2x decode throughput gains; up to 1.8x P90 interactivity on AgentX
Unified CuTe DSL decode path: attention, MoE, communication
Admission: agent-generated code outpaces human review
Argues for automatic verification systems alongside agentic optimization
